fatal_errors: A roughly 300 mm nozzle-to-substrate distance is geometrically incompatible with deposition inside a 120 mm internal diameter and therefore does not satisfy a central design constraint.
The proposed intervention misses the target process change: 5–30 μm powder and optimization of the i7 air/fuel-pressure setting with the 63 mm 3L4 nozzle and 2.75 mm injector.
The claimed argon-shielded HVAF environment, fuel/oxygen tuning, and at least 30% thickness gain are not supported by the cited evidence.
The proposed service boundary of approximately 900 °C fails to address the demonstrated 1000–1150 °C oxidation regime.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses insufficient thickness and gives a reasonable generic mechanism: shorter stand-off can preserve particle velocity, reduce oxidation, and improve deposition. E1 supports only these qualitative stand-off trends. It does not establish 300 mm as optimal for the i7 torch, a 30% thickness increase, an inert atmosphere, or adequate adhesion. More importantly, the proposed stand-off cannot practically address a 120 mm internal diameter. The hidden target instead uses finer 5–30 μm feedstock and an optimized medium air/fuel-pressure i7 configuration to produce an approximately 150 μm coating with 79% deposition efficiency and 0.2% porosity. The generated answer also omits the target's protective-alumina/sluggish-diffusion mechanism and its 50 h oxidation evidence at 1000–1150 °C. Its controlled distance comparison and explicit falsification criterion are useful, although the 30% threshold and assumed baseline above 350 mm are arbitrary.
